source_quote: The engineer opens the ontology agent and ensures they are in plan mode. Like a draft mode. They prompt the agent with specific instructions. Add a sale entity using the sales table in the sales report semantic model located in this specific workspace. Okay, very specific. They then ask the agent to preview the proposed definition, show exactly how it mapped the data bindings and explain the source evidence it used to make those decisions, all while keeping the rest of the live ontology completely untouched. So Plan Mode operates as a secure sandbox. Exactly. It is a critical enterprise safety feature. Plan Mode allows you to discover, draft, validate, query, and inspect massive structural changes without actually altering the live production ontology that the rest of the company is currently using. You can test it out first. You can see the draft entity appear on the visual canvas, check how it mapped the primary and foreign keys, and run validation checks. If you realize the AI agent picked the wrong column for the primary key or completely missed a crucial relationship, you can ask for revisions right there in the sandbox, or manually adjust it yourself. And when you are finally satisfied that the logic holds up. Then and only then do you deliberately switch the interface to ACT mode to apply the reviewed proposal, merging it into the live model.
